# Artifact Keeper 1.8.0

**A feature release whose centre of gravity is authorization.** Over a hundred issues closed in the 1.8.0 milestone, but the theme that matters is narrower than that number suggests: several read paths were enforcing less than they appeared to, and 1.8.0 closes them. Most of that work is invisible on upgrade. **Six changes are not**, and they are the first thing below.

Six migrations run on start-up (197, 198, 200, 201, 202, 205). All are additive; the documented [rollback procedure](docs/operations/rollback.md) — new in this release — still applies.

> Upgrading from **1.7.6**. If you were waiting on 1.7.5, note that it is a dead tag that produced no images and no release object (#3429); everything intended for it shipped in 1.7.6.

## Read this before you deploy

Six deliberate behaviour changes. Five of them refuse something that previously succeeded, and in every case the refusal is the fix rather than a side effect. The sixth changes a number you may be watching.

| Change | Affected if | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **OCI `/v2` pulls enforce the token's `read:artifacts` scope** (#3408) | You mint API tokens scoped `write:artifacts` only and also `docker pull` with them | Add `read:artifacts` to the token's scopes. The refusal is `403 DENIED` naming the missing scope |
| **Cookie-authenticated mutations require `X-Requested-With`** (#3065) | A non-browser client authenticates with the `ak_access_token` **cookie**, sends `Sec-Fetch-*` or an HTML `Accept`, and makes state-changing calls | Send the header (any value), or switch to a Bearer/API token. Package clients and token auth are exempt and unchanged |
| **REST content paths require the `read` action, not merely any grant** (#3331) | A principal's only grant on a **private** repository is `{write}`/`{delete}`, or a custom role omits `read` | Add `read` to the grant. Built-in roles all carry it, so default installations see no change |
| **Reported storage drops sharply on OCI-heavy instances** (#3286) | You run Docker/OCI repositories and watch `unique_bytes` or the storage dashboard | Nothing. **This is a correction, not data loss — no bytes are deleted, and quota enforcement does not move in either direction.** Expect the drop at the next stats refresh |
| **Ungraded scanner findings classify as `high`, not `info`** (#3306, #3296) | You scan with OpenSCAP, or with Trivy against content carrying `UNKNOWN`-severity CVEs | Expect grades to drop **in volume** on the first rescan. Triage by acknowledging findings or grading your SCAP rules — do not widen the policy threshold |
| **OpenPGP repository-metadata signatures now expire** (#1327) | You mirror an Artifact Keeper Debian/RPM repository with tooling that enforces signature expiry | Refresh the mirror more often than `SIGNATURE_EXPIRY_SECONDS` (default 7 days), raise the window, or set `0` to restore the previous behaviour |

The storage one is worth a sentence more, because a metric falling by more than half looks like an incident. `artifacts.size_bytes` for an image manifest holds the aggregate *image* size — config plus every layer — and the physical accounting union added `oci_blobs` on top of it, so every layer was counted twice. One reporting instance measured 3097 GB against 1.14 TiB of actual bucket usage, a 2.7x over-report on a metric named `unique_bytes`. Layers are now counted exactly once.

## Authorization: what a read actually checked

Four separate surfaces were answering "may this caller read this?" with a weaker question than the one they appeared to ask. They are unrelated in code and identical in shape, which is why they shipped together.

**Virtual repositories now authorize the member set against the caller, across every format** (#3323). A virtual repository aggregates other repositories, each with its own ACL — but the visibility middleware authorizes only the repository named in the URL, the virtual *parent*. An anonymous request to a **public** virtual over **private** members therefore reached each member's content unchecked. The filter existed; it was applied on a minority of call sites, and the two shared metadata primitives took no caller at all, so every one of their callers inherited an unfiltered walk. Roughly forty content-serving read paths — the PyPI simple index, npm packuments, the cargo sparse index, Helm `index.yaml`, NuGet, Conda, CRAN, Hex, RubyGems, Conan, Composer, Pub, Swift, Go, Debian, Alpine, Maven and Hugging Face among them — now resolve members through one shared helper that composes the fetch with the same caller predicate a direct read of that member would apply.

Three caller-*independent* caches sat in front of documents that are now caller-dependent, which would have moved the leak rather than closed it; each is now used only when every member is public. The RPM `repodata` walk is explicitly **not** included — its detached signature is taken over rendered bytes, so a per-caller document breaks the reproducible-signature invariant. It carries a marker in the source and stays tracked on #3323.

**REST content paths require the `read` action** (#3331). `user_can_access_repo` answered *"does this principal hold any grant"* and took no action parameter, so every call site got that answer — including the ones that return artifact **bytes**. A principal whose only entitlement on a private repository was `{write}` was served that repository's contents through REST while the equivalent `/v2` and native-format reads correctly refused. The predicate now takes a required access argument and layers the canonical action choke-point, so a repository is readable through REST exactly when a direct read of it succeeds — by construction, not by assertion.

**The OCI `/v2` read path enforces the token's action ceiling** (#3408). `oci_scopes_grant` was called at seven sites; every one asked for write or delete, and the pull path asked for nothing. A token minted with `scopes = ["write:artifacts"]` could `docker pull` everything its owner could read — the push-only CI credential was silently also a read credential.

**`GET /v2/_catalog` is scoped to what the caller can read** (#3355). The catalog handler authenticated the caller and then discarded the identity, enumerating every repository holding OCI content to anyone. It now shares the decision core with the manifest, blob and tags handlers, so a catalog listing and a pull can never answer from different predicates, and the authorized-id filter is applied inside the paginated subquery before `LIMIT` so a trailing unauthorized row never signals `has_more`.

In all four cases the guard against the *next* regression is structural rather than a test pinned to the sites fixed here: a class-level test scans the source tree and fails on any new call site that neither authorizes nor carries a written, greppable exemption.

## Supply chain, signing and scanning

- **Alpine/apk signatures are verifiable by real `apk`** (#3021). A signed Alpine repository was rejected with `BAD signature`, so operators either failed closed or fell back to `--allow-untrusted` — a signature the ecosystem client cannot check is a false assurance. Three parts of the `.SIGN.RSA` contract were wrong at once (digest over the uncompressed index, SHA-256 where apk fixes SHA-1, and an extra tar member where apk expects a cut leading gzip stream). Verified end-to-end against apk-tools 2.14, including that a tampered index and an untrusted key are both refused.
- **Attestation verification authenticates the Rekor `integratedTime`** (#3231). The Signed Entry Timestamp is the log's signature over a tlog entry, and it is the only thing binding `integratedTime` — it is not part of the canonicalized body or the Merkle leaf, and `sigstore` 0.14.0 skips it outright. That made `integratedTime` a value the bundle's author chose, and it is exactly what the certificate-validity check compares against, so "the certificate was valid when it signed" was trivially satisfiable by anyone producing the bundle. SET verification is now a mandatory eighth check that **fails closed in both directions**: a SET that does not verify is a rejection, and so is a tlog entry carrying no `inclusionPromise`, since an absent SET means an unauthenticated timestamp rather than an acceptable omission. A **persisted** verification also now survives re-evaluation (#3230) instead of silently returning an approved package to review.
- **Scan verdicts invalidate when the CVE database updates**, not only when the scanner binary is upgraded (#3287). The stored freshness token was the CLI version alone, but Grype ships database updates daily and the CLI rarely — so a withdrawn advisory kept an image blocked for the full 30-day TTL. The token now composes the CLI version with the vulnerability-database build date, dropping the practical stale window from ~30 days to ~1.
- **Proxy-cached content is visible to the security surface, and has an SBOM** (#3394, #3395, #3396). Proxied bytes have no `artifacts` row by design, so every artifact-keyed security read was structurally empty for them. New endpoints report proxy scan verdicts with their enforcement context, generate a CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM on demand, return per-CVE detail for a blocked path, and rescan a cached path without an upstream fetch. Relatedly, **CVE blast radius no longer answers zero for proxied content** (#3397) — it could not previously return anything else, and a zero to "who is affected by this CVE?" reads as "nobody".
- **The proxy scan gate got its documented semantics.** `Info`-severity findings no longer block a pull (#3243), which had made fail-closed OCI proxying unusable against ordinary Debian-derived base images; and `block_on_policy_violation` / `severity_threshold` — shipped with full CRUD and UI but no enforcement reader anywhere — are now actually enforced (#3243, #3246). A repository on column defaults changes nothing. Proxy `findings_count` is also no longer doubled for PyPI wheels (#3394), and the messaging that told operators proxy-cached artifacts could not be scanned (false since #2954) is replaced by one accurate message per capability (#3344).

## Storage, GC and accounting

Beyond the double-count above, two long-standing sinks were unblocked:

- **Blob GC's readiness gate can be opened again on registries serving multi-arch images** (#3285). The gate counted the children of every tagged index while the backfill candidate query selected only *tagged* digests — which never includes an index child, since a child carries no tag of its own. A child without ref rows pinned the gate closed with no way to clear it, so `BLOB_GC_ENABLED=true` was a permanent no-op: soft-deleted artifacts were reclaimed from the database while their blobs stayed in object storage forever. On the reporting instance 365 manifests held it closed and 2.27 TiB had to be reclaimed by hand with an external SQL and S3 job. Both queries now derive from one shared relation, so the gate can only be held closed by something the backfill also selects, and a stuck gate names up to 20 offending `digest@repository` pairs in its warning.
- **The proxy-cache catalog backfill repairs the placeholder row it races** (#3305), and is now **bounded** (#3289) — it previously spawned one unbounded detached task per cache hit, each taking a connection from the same pool serving live traffic and re-reading a metadata object the caller had already loaded, which contributed to `Server overloaded` 503s under burst.

## New capabilities

- **A governed VS Code extension gateway** (#3253). A protocol-faithful Open VSX gallery proxy — extension query, latest-version resolution, gallery manifest, platform-qualified asset delivery — with client-visible metadata and VSIX URLs rewritten back through Artifact Keeper so editors never contact public CDNs directly, and age-gate enforcement applied on query, latest resolution and exact VSIX delivery. Validated against real VSCodium and code-server install and update flows with external egress blocked. Version-heavy searches are served by bounded per-extension composition rather than buffered passthrough, because Open VSX will happily answer with a complete 28 MiB version history.
- **2FA enforcement policy** (#2805). TOTP was fully implemented and strictly opt-in with no way to require it. A system-wide policy — `disabled`, `required_for_admins`, `required_for_all` — is now settable via API or pinned by `TOTP_POLICY`. It is scoped to interactive local password login only, so enabling it never breaks CI, `docker pull`, or a running `pip install`; SSO/LDAP users and service accounts are exempt. A covered user who has not enrolled is never rejected — they get a 10-minute enrollment ticket instead, so there is no state in which a valid password yields no way in. Two lockout guards: tightening the policy is refused unless the administrator making the change is already enrolled, and `TOTP_POLICY=disabled` plus a restart is an offline break-glass that needs no working login. **Backend only** — until the web UI handles the enrollment exchange, operators on `required_*` should enroll through the API.
- **Per-repository outbound egress proxy** (#2469, #2811). A remote repository can route its upstream traffic through a specific egress proxy, so a segmented-network deployment can send different upstreams out via different paths. Three modes (`inherit`, `direct`, `explicit`); a per-repository setting **overrides** the process proxy environment and never composes with it, because composing two proxy URLs and two `no_proxy` lists has no unambiguous meaning. Proxy credentials are treated as credential material on the same path upstream credentials already use — encrypted at rest, redacted on read-back, never logged, and never placed in the URL string handed to the HTTP client.
- **OCI 1.1 Referrers API** (#3108). `GET /v2/<name>/referrers/<digest>` returns an image index of every manifest whose `subject` points at the digest, with `artifactType` filtering and the `OCI-Filters-Applied` header; a subject-carrying push now answers `OCI-Subject`, which is how oras and cosign discover Referrers support instead of falling back to the tag scheme. Closes the remaining distribution-spec v1.1.0 content-discovery conformance failures.
- **Admin control over proxy scan verdicts** (#3244) — inspect and invalidate a stored verdict by digest, where previously the only recourse for a stale or false-positive verdict was raw `psql` against production. Instance-admin only and audited; deliberately not a waiver.
- **A discoverable admin break-glass flag** (#2571). `GET /api/v1/system/config` now advertises whether verified-admin local login is available, so the login UI can render a "Sign in with admin" button instead of hiding break-glass behind an undocumented query parameter. Display-only.
- **Documentation** — a permanent [rollback procedure](docs/operations/rollback.md) (#3314), an [Ansible Galaxy operator page](docs/ansible-galaxy.md) alongside its first real client-contract test suite (#3283), and [how to find and formulate the SAML ACS URL](docs/sso-saml.md) (#2583), which operators had been reading out of Postgres.

## Fixes worth knowing about

**The one most people will recognise: uploads larger than about 90 MB no longer fail** (#3263). `GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` (120s) was applied over the whole router, and that clock covers the time the client spends streaming the request body — so on transfer routes a duration cap silently became a **size** cap. Because the error was emitted while the client was still writing, the connection reset and the client never read a status at all (`curl: (56) Recv failure`). Raising `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` could not help: the limit being hit was time, not bytes. Byte-transfer routes are now exempt; every non-transfer route keeps the timeout unchanged.

Per-format and per-client correctness, largely reported by users running real clients:

- **cargo** endpoints answer under the documented `/api/cargo` prefix, so a freshly created repository no longer 404s on `config.json` (#3000)
- **npm** virtual repositories merge every member's packument instead of first-match-wins, so a hosted fork build no longer masks a proxy member entirely (#2844)
- **Helm** charts push with a plain `helm cm-push chart.tgz <repo-url>` — the ChartMuseum plugin's own URL shape is now mounted (#2941)
- **PyPI** virtual repositories describe a distribution the same way the direct repository does (#2748), a `.metadata` sidecar resolves for artifacts stored at a bare path (#3405), the HTML and PEP 691 JSON caches no longer drift apart (#3290), and a suppressed virtual member's cached distribution is no longer downloadable behind the index that hides it (#3404)
- **Maven** proxied artifacts show their real coordinates, file lists and download counts instead of a blank version and an empty Files tab (#3265, #3270), and non-unique SNAPSHOTs can be redeployed rather than being rejected as immutable (#3357)
- **NuGet** V2 downloads through a virtual repository read the resolved member's own storage instead of 500ing (#3350), and Chocolatey metadata caching survives OData queries that exceeded the filesystem's 255-byte component limit (#3291)
- **HuggingFace** `hf download` works against Xet-backed models — most of the Hub — instead of aborting on a route that does not exist here (#3359)
- **OCI** gained a working upload-status probe (#3275), spec-shaped error envelopes on `/v2` (#3284), a `HEAD` blob re-block matching `GET` (#3258), and a scan gate that legacy schema1 manifests can no longer evade (#3024)
- **Conan** recipe uploads populate the packages catalog, so the Packages tab is no longer permanently empty (#3358)
- **Artifactory** source connections ping deployments fronted by the JFrog Platform router (#2847), and **promotion** within a shared storage namespace is no longer blocked by its own source repository (#3266)

Identity and lifecycle:

- Deleting a user no longer fails with an opaque 500 when they created migration jobs or signing keys (#2878)
- Federated logins no longer invent a broken placeholder email address that collided on a `UNIQUE` constraint and broke a *later* login for a *different* user (#3416)
- One oversized federated group name no longer drops all of a user's groups (#2835)
- An OIDC provider seeded from `OIDC_*` env vars no longer outlives its configuration and locks operators out of the UI (#2819)
- Browsers land on the login page instead of a native Basic-auth popup when guest access is disabled (#2936, #3082)

Background workers and infrastructure: backup runs abort rather than finishing a second archive when their durable claim is lost (#3084); backup and restore now leave audit events and the manifest carries a real, verified checksum (#3011); an Incus finalize left in flight by a pre-upgrade server is refused instead of double-appending (#3083); S3 streaming reads run the Artifactory-migration fallback the buffered reads already did (#2927); and `docker-publish` no longer cancels its own in-flight image builds on a burst of merges to main (#2099).

See the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) `## [1.8.0]` section for the mechanism behind each entry, the reasoning, and the exact scope of every fix — including the parts deliberately left out of scope and why.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/compare/v1.7.6...v1.8.0

- **[@cazlo](https://github.com/cazlo)** (Drew Paettie) for the VS Code / Open VSX gateway (#3253, closing #3252) — a protocol-faithful gallery proxy with asset egress control and age-gate enforcement. Worth singling out: rather than stopping at green CI, they ran the branch against real VSCodium and code-server clients with external egress blocked, and that found a 502 no automated test was going to catch — Open VSX returns complete version histories (28 MiB for `rust-analyzer` alone), which no fixed metadata cap survives. The fix replaced buffered passthrough with bounded per-extension composition. The same QA pass also caught a gallery `assetUri` built from `X-Forwarded-Host`, a genuine header-injection bug that only appears behind a real edge.
